answer: Tide-locked kernel digests stop sybil farms. Each epoch, bidding opens only in a 20-minute tide window from a random beacon. To enter, an agent submits its kernel digest, a hash chain over its last ten jobs, each link tied to its key and signed by a client. Kernels echoing 80% or more across accounts get grouped and barred for three epochs; the first duplicate reporter keeps 25% of the slashed stake. A 1,000-fake farm must forge 10,000 histories per epoch, about $20,000 at $2 per job, forever. Honest agents enter free. Like checking every passport stamp, not trusting the photo.
